about: The Fasteners bridge's tools for agents (through Agent Link), listed only when Fasteners Workbench is installed: name, what it does, its arguments as JSON Schema, its group, whether it changes the document.

fastener_types.description: Read the types, sizes and lengths of Fasteners Workbench, from its own tables. These tools are listed only when Fasteners Workbench is installed. There are three levels. No type: the answer holds the types that match query, standard and kind. query is words, and all must match ("socket cap"). standard: ISO, DIN, ASME …. kind: screw, nut, washer, insert, pin …. The answer then holds count and types [{ type, kind, what }]: the first 40; narrow the query for more. type ("ISO4762"): the answer holds the sizes of that type ["M3", …] and hasLength. type and size: the answer holds lengths, hole and insert. lengths: the lengths it comes in, or length { any, default } for one cut to length. hole: the pass and tap hole diameters from Fasteners' own screw calculator. insert: the hole and depth of an IUT heat-set insert. A type that is not one is refused not_found, with the nearest names. A size that the type does not come in is refused, with the sizes it does. Sizes are written as Fasteners writes them (M3, #10, 1/4in). Changes nothing. Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer.
fastener_types.source: Workshop for FreeCAD (Fasteners bridge), calling Fasteners Workbench at run time

fastener_add.description: Add a Fasteners Workbench part (screw, bolt, nut, washer, insert, pin …). type (required): the type name of Fasteners, for example ISO4762 (fastener_types { query } finds one). edges: round edges; one fastener is attached to each. Give an edge as "Plate.Edge7", or as { body, near: [x, y, z] }. near is a point on the round edge or at the centre of the hole, within 1 mm. At a centre, the nearest centre wins, then the outer rim of the hole. Prefer near: edge numbers change after any edit of the body. Without edges, it is made loose at at [x, y, z] (the origin when left out). size: M3. size wins over the hole; left out on edges, Fasteners matches it to the diameter of the edge. length: mm (the nearest length the type comes in). thread simple (the default): a plain cylinder, fast. thread real: a modelled thread, slow and heavy, for close-ups only. match outer (default): the edge is a pass hole, and the screw goes through. match inner: a tap hole, and its thread fits it. invert: true turns it end for end. offset: mm along its axis. On an edge, it is seated. Seated: its head is on the open side of the edge. The head of a nut or washer is its face; the head of an insert is its top. The shank goes into the material, whichever way FreeCAD's circle for that edge points. Fasteners puts the head where the axis of the circle points. On a PartDesign Hole, that can be into the plate. invert: true turns it end for end from seated. The shape cannot always tell the open side (a rim with material on both sides). Then it is as Fasteners places it. A size given on the wall of a counterbore goes on the edge of the bore at its floor. attachNote says so. Kept on its hole: each attached fastener also keeps the geometry of the edge (centre, axis, radius). A later PartDesign feature can renumber the edges of the Body. The fastener is then put back on the same round edge (reattached). When no edge of that size is left within reach, it stays where it is and says so. It is then lost, with a Report-view warning; fastener_set { edge } puts it on another. Labels read "M8x25-Screw", "M8x25-Screw 2" …, numbered per size and kept. Fasteners itself relabels at every recompute. Refused: an unknown type (the nearest names are given). Refused: a size that the type does not come in. Refused: an edge that is not circular. Refused: a point with no round edge within 1 mm (the nearest are listed). Refused: thread or match other than their two words. The answer holds: made [{ object, label, type, kind, size, length, thread (simple | real), matchOuter, invert (Fasteners' own Invert), offset, attachedTo ("Plate.Edge7"), edgeDiameter, headSide (open side, or in the material when turned end for end), shankOut (mm the shank stands out of the hole's far rim: a screw longer than its hole), at, bom (its BOM line), hidden, attachNote, hole (kept | reattached | lost), reattached, lost, adopted }], source. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check. Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer.

edges.description: Round edges: "Plate.Edge7", or { body, near: [x, y, z] }: a point on the round edge, or the hole's centre (within 1 mm of either; at a centre, the nearest centre, then the hole's outer rim).

fastener_add.source: Workshop for FreeCAD (Fasteners bridge), calling Fasteners Workbench at run time

fastener_set.description: Change Fasteners parts in place, as Fasteners' own Change Parameters, Flip and Move do. Each part keeps its object name and label. objects (required unless only restore): names or labels (fastener_list gives them). Give any of these inputs. type: only one with the same properties, for example a screw to another screw standard. Another type is refused, with a list of what it can become. size: "Auto" matches it to its hole again. length: mm (the nearest it comes in). thread: simple | real. invert: true turns it end for end from seated, with its head into the material. invert: false seats it, with its head on the open side. offset: mm. match: inner | outer. edge ("Plate.Edge9") moves it to another round edge, seated there. It is turned end for end there only when it was before, or when invert says so. label: for ONE fastener, the label that it then keeps across recomputes. With several objects, label is refused. restore: true gives the Fasteners objects of the document their behaviour back. Use it when the file was saved where Fasteners Workbench was not loaded. restore alone needs no objects; the answer holds restored. Refused: no objects. Refused: an object that is not a Fasteners part. Refused: a type that it cannot become, or a size that it does not come in. The answer holds: changed [{ object, label, type, kind, size, length, thread (simple | real), matchOuter, invert (Fasteners' own Invert), offset, attachedTo ("Plate.Edge7"), edgeDiameter, headSide (open side, or in the material when turned end for end), shankOut, at, bom (its BOM line), hidden, attachNote, hole (kept | reattached | lost), reattached, lost, adopted }]. shankOut: mm the shank stands out of the far rim of the hole. That is a length longer than the hole, as a 20 mm screw in a 10 mm plate. A changed fastener can still be "not recomputed yet" after its last step, and not before the call. It is then recomputed once more, so the health check of the next call does not list it. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check. Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer.

label.description: One fastener's label, kept as given across recomputes (Fasteners' own relabelling is undone).

fastener_set.source: Workshop for FreeCAD (Fasteners bridge), calling Fasteners Workbench at run time

fastener_list.description: List the Fasteners parts in the document and their bill of materials. They are counted from the objects as they are now. The answer holds: fasteners [{ object, label, type, kind, size, length, thread (simple | real), matchOuter, invert, offset, attachedTo ("Plate.Edge7"), edgeDiameter, at, bom (its BOM line), hidden, attachNote, hole (kept | reattached | lost), reattached, lost, adopted }] and bom [{ item ("ISO4762 Screw M3x12"), qty }]. Each fastener is listed once, hidden ones too (hidden: true). The links and arrays of it that Fasteners counts are listed too. Before listing, each attached fastener is checked against its hole. hole kept: on its hole. reattached: put back on the same circle after FreeCAD renumbered the edges. lost: its hole moved or was removed. A lost fastener is also under warnings; fastener_set { edge } puts it on one. Fasteners from before Workshop kept them are taken in as the document opens or recomputes. They come from older documents, or were added with Fasteners' own buttons. Their hole comes from the edge they are on. A label that Fasteners counted up is put back in the per-size scheme. adopted: true says so. sheet: true also puts the BOM in a spreadsheet in the document. With the window up, that is Fasteners' own Generate BOM; else it is Workshop's, in the same layout. That call changes the document, and the answer adds sheet and by. Without sheet, it is a read. The reattaching above is the keeper's own doing, not this call's. Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer.
fastener_list.source: Workshop for FreeCAD (Fasteners bridge), calling Fasteners Workbench at run time

fastener_print.description: Read or set the 3D-print thread settings of Fasteners Workbench. They are its own preference, for every document on this computer, and they are not kept with the file. Called with nothing, it only reads them: mode (standard | 3dprint), nut [A, B], screw [A, B], formula, source. The diameter of a printed thread is d x A + B. nut is for inside threads (1.03, 0.1 to start). screw is for outside threads (0.99, −0.05). They apply when mode is 3dprint. Give mode, nut [A, B] and/or screw [A, B] to set them. Every fastener with a real (modelled) thread in every open document is then recomputed and named under redone. This is slow when there are many. Refused: a mode other than the two. Refused: nut or screw that is not two numbers. When mode is 3dprint, the modelled threads of thread_cut in a printed body take the nut figures as their clearance. history_undo does not undo it: it is a preference, not part of the document. Call it again with the old figures. Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer.
